newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses fall, hit by Wall St sell-off.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses fall, hit by Wall St sell-off.

text.p: European stocks fell sharply in early trading on Friday, dragged down by an overnight wave of selling on Wall Street because of jitters over interest rates and a weakening dollar.

On currency markets, the dollar drifted lower against the mark after stronger-than-expected German economic data on Thursday dampened speculation of a cut in interest rates and boosted the German currency.
London, Frankfurt and Paris, which have all hit peaks in recent weeks. showed big losses within minutes of opening after New York posted a 1.32 percent decline at the close on Thursday.
"The feeling is that we are very much at the top of the range and the market is going to be volatile," said one dealer in London.
Europe's major bourses, which have largely mirrored the bull run in New York, were rattled after the Dow Jones industrial average ended down 92.75 points at 6,927.38 on Thursday.
Wall Street's weakness came only two days after it set a record high of 7,067.46. Investors became nervous about an upturn in long-term interest rates and the weaker dollar.

The currency's recent strength has been an important factor in the stock market's rally. It has drawn considerable investment to U.S. financial markets from outside the country. Frankfurt was the hardest hit by Wall Street. The computerised IBIS index fell by one percent in pre-bourse deals, with sentiment also depressed by the softer dollar which could harm German exports.

"There seems to be wholesale selling across the board this morning and the big heavyweights, like the chemical companies and Daimler Benz are all down," said one Frankfurt trader. By mid-morning, the IBIS was still showing a loss of 0.77 percent. Floor trade was down by a similar margin on the DAX index.
In Paris, stocks retreated at the opening after the Wall Street slide, with almost every stock in the CAC-40 leading share index turning downwards.
Dealers said the market, already consolidating for two days, had been expected to slip further on Friday, monthly settlement day. The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 0.63 percent by mid-morning.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, recovered some poise and was showing a loss of only 0.3 percent at mid-session.

Among individual stocks, shares in GKN Plc advanced 29-1/2p to 956 after the engineering group said late on Thursday that possible damages from a lawsuit brought by its U.S. franchising operation could fall by 30 percent or more.

On the currency front, the dollar was down on Thursday's closing levels as expectations diminished of near-term German interest rate cuts and attitudes to the yen turned cautiously more positive, analysts said.

"The bias is towards a firmer mark in the aftermath of yesterday's (German) numbers...running parallel is the more positive yen sentiment that is prevailing in Japan," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered in London.

On the yen side, senior Japanese Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara said overnight that foreigners had been buying yen since February 20, and forex rates had been "rather stable" since the G7 meeting of leading industrial countries this month.
With a day short on trading incentives, the dollar may edge lower but on a broader canvas the market still prefers the dollar bullish scenario, analysts said.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6853 marks and 122.70 yen compared to the 1.6895 and 123.07 in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 13.3 points at 4,342.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 13.94 points at 2,561.30.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 22.19 points at 3,173.84.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened stronger at $351.20, compared with $346.45 at the London close on Thursday.
